## Windows: a corrected recovery line, and what a refused start looks like

**Windows only.** The Linux package changes only in its version number.

**What was wrong.** When the service refuses a credential folder that nothing vouches for (0.24.1 and later), the message it writes to the Windows Application log tells you, if Windows will not let you delete the folder, to run `takeown /F "<folder>" /A /R /D Y`. The `/D` option takes the letter for "yes" of the language of Windows, so on every Windows that is not English the `Y` is rejected with a syntax error and the line does nothing. It now says `takeown /F "<folder>" /A /R`, and that takeown may ask a yes/no question in the language of Windows: answer yes.

**What else changes in that message.** A folder the service cannot list counts as not empty. An empty folder whose owner took SYSTEM out of its permissions was refused with "is not empty" and sent whoever read it looking for files that are not there; the message now says why, and `observer doctor` says that the service does not replace such a folder. The recovery is the same three `icacls` lines as for any refused folder, in the [README](https://github.com/Akr0n/observer#packages) under *Packages*.

**What a refusal looks like, measured.** On a real machine, with the recovery actions the package sets (restart after five seconds) applied by hand to a throwaway service, Windows did not retry a refused start in the 40 seconds that were watched: starting the service waited about 30 seconds and failed with error 1053, and the reason was in the Application log (source `.NET Runtime`, event 1026) and nowhere the System log points to. The service stayed stopped for as long as it was watched, so plan on starting it yourself once the folder is fixed. Not tried: a service that crashes after it has started, the start at boot, and an MSI upgrade that rolls back with error 1920.

**No action needed.** Nothing about the token, the certificate or who can read them changes.
